taxonomy_metadata.name: slop-detector v2 LLM-judge rubric
taxonomy_metadata.methodology: Condensed adaptation of StoryScope's 304-feature narrative taxonomy (research/storyscope_taxonomy.json) to general-prose slop detection. StoryScope scores HOW a story is built across 10 dimensions; we keep that philosophy but reduce to 14 questions one judge call can score per document.
design_constraints: One LLM call per document; whole rubric must fit a system prompt (<1200 words). See research/taxonomy_v2_system_prompt.txt.
Covers HOW text is built (structure/narrative/discourse), not word tics -- surface tics stay in ontology/patterns.core.yaml regex lanes.
Must be register-agnostic where possible: fiction, QA answers, wiki intros, reddit/blogs prose, arxiv paraphrases.
Output conventions mirror scripts/label_v2_llm.py: single JSON object, verdict/confidence/rubric/spans.

registers.web: wiki intros, reddit posts, blog prose

taxonomy_metadata.scale_convention: All questions scored 0-4 by the judge unless noted. slop_direction 'high' means higher score => more AI-like; 'low' means lower score => more AI-like.

questions.question: How uniform are paragraph lengths and internal structure (0=highly varied and purposeful, 4=all paragraphs near-identical size and shape)?
questions.detection_method: Compare paragraph lengths and openings across the doc; check whether each paragraph plays a distinct rhetorical role or whether they rhythmically repeat (setup, elaboration, wrap). Uniform machine-gun paragraphs score high.

questions.question: How much variance is there in sentence length and syntax (0=monotone even sentences, 4=wild, purposeful mix of fragments, long runs, short punches)?
questions.detection_method: Sample 15-20 sentences; estimate the spread between shortest and longest and how often syntax repeats subject-verb-object. Human prose bursts; LLM prose glides at a steady clip. Low variance scores low.

questions.question: How heavily does the text lean on lists, triads, and parallel constructions ('X, Y, and Z' rhythms, bullet-like enumeration in prose) beyond what content requires (0=organic, 4=pervasive)?
questions.detection_method: Count rule-of-three groupings, semicolon chains, and grammatically parallel clause strings per paragraph; rate whether they feel motivated by content or inserted as filler symmetry. Pervasive unforced parallelism scores high.

questions.question: How concrete is the detail (0=vague abstraction throughout, 4=rich specific names, numbers, sensory particulars)?
questions.detection_method: Check whether claims and scenes are anchored in specifics (real nouns, quantities, sensory detail) or float on abstractions ('various factors', 'a sense of wonder'). Vague-generic texture scores low.

questions.question: How evenly calibrated is the emotional temperature (0=genuinely uneven, surging or flat where content demands, 4=tastefully modulated everywhere, never too hot or cold)?
questions.detection_method: Judge whether emotional intensity tracks the events or sits at a constant pleasant middle register; note tell-over-feel moves like naming emotions ('she felt a mixture of excitement and apprehension'). Constant tasteful modulation scores high.

questions.question: How strong is an individual authorial voice (0=no discernible person behind the words, 4=distinct opinions, quirks, stake, idiosyncrasies)?
questions.detection_method: Ask: could this plausibly be anyone? Look for personal stance, humor, asymmetries, willingness to be odd or wrong. Interchangeable competent-neutral voice scores low. (Wiki intros legitimately lack voice; grade relative to register norm.)

questions.question: How formulaic are transitions and signposting ('Moreover', 'In conclusion', 'It's important to note', 'Let's delve into') relative to register norms (0=natural flow, 4=textbook scaffolding everywhere)?
questions.detection_method: List transition words and meta-discourse phrases at paragraph and section boundaries; judge whether they carry real logical weight or are decorative connective tissue. Dense stock scaffolding scores high.

questions.question: How saturated is the text in balanced hedging ('can vary', 'may depend', 'it's worth noting', on-the-one-hand framing) beyond genuine uncertainty (0=commits to claims appropriately, 4=hedges everything symmetrically)?
questions.detection_method: Count hedge constructions and both-sides balances; ask whether the hedging reflects actual epistemic state or reflexive caution. Blanket symmetric hedging absent real stakes scores high.

questions.question: How much does the text restate what it already said (mini-summaries, 'in other words' loops, conclusion restating intro verbatim-ish) (0=tight, additive prose, 4=heavy redundancy)?
questions.detection_method: Track propositional content; flag passages whose information was already delivered earlier, especially intro-conclusion mirroring and end-of-paragraph recaps. High redundant restatement scores high.

questions.question: How even is narrative pacing across scenes (0=dramatically varied -- acceleration, dilation, jump-cuts driven by story logic, 4=steady metronome coverage event after event)?
questions.detection_method: Map time-to-text ratio across the piece; humans compress and dilate unevenly around turning points, LLM narrators allot similar space to each beat. Metronome coverage scores high.

questions.question: How deep and specific is character interiority (0=no inner life or generic labeled feelings, 4=particular, contradictory, oblique thought)?
questions.detection_method: Collect every passage inside a character's head; check whether thoughts are specific, tangled, and oblique or generic named emotions stated flatly ('he was nervous', 'she felt determined'). Generic or absent interiority scores low.

questions.question: Does the piece dramatize (scene: dialogue, concrete moment, real-time action) or summarize (0=largely vivid scene, 4=almost entirely told summary/reportage)?
questions.detection_method: Classify each major beat as scene (unfolds in real time with sensory/dialogue grounding) or summary (events recounted). A story that tells its events rather than staging them scores high.

questions.question: How neatly does the ending resolve (0=messy, partial, or resonant-without-summary ending, 4=bows tied: lesson stated, arc closed, final line lands like a stamp)?
questions.detection_method: Read only the last two paragraphs: does it close every opened thread, moralize, or echo the opening? Over-resolved, lesson-delivering endings score high.

questions.question: How dense are stock phrases, dead metaphors, and expected collocations ('little did she know', 'testament to', 'tapestry', 'delve') per 100 words (0=fresh phrasing, 4=cliché-saturated)?
questions.detection_method: Underline every phrase you predicted before reading it; estimate density of predictable collocations and worn figurative language against the doc's length and register. High predicted-phrase density scores high.

register_variant_map.comment: Which questions the judge should answer per register. Questions outside the map are skipped (return null) to keep scoring fair across registers.

output_schema.description: Single JSON object per document, no prose. Conventions match scripts/label_v2_llm.py SYSTEM block (verdict/confidence/spans) extended with the rubric dict keyed by question id.

verdict.notes: 'mixed' only if the doc genuinely interleaves human and AI prose

confidence.notes: calibrated certainty in the verdict, not average rubric score

rubric.keys: question ids applicable to the register (see register_variant_map); unanswered questions omitted or null

items.quote: verbatim substring of the doc, <=200 chars
items.why: one-clause reason citing the question id or pattern
